**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — INDEMN.**

- **What the document says:** Article XII (p0128–p0129) is a one-way indemnity running against us, covering our exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business, and any breach. There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and Article XIII (p0130) expressly states that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT," on top of the non-infringement warranty disclaimer.
- **Why it fails:** This is the rule's walk-away scenario (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity); it does not even reach the fallback, which requires at minimum a Vendor IP indemnity.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a new Article XII-A Licensor indemnity for third-party IP claims, Licensor's breach of law, Licensor-caused data/confidentiality incidents, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and an express carve-out from Article XIII; and narrowed our own indemnity to Licensee-provided content, our breach of law, and our breach of the Agreement (also fixing the "the License" typo). The comment offers the fallback (usual IP exclusions/remedies plus a 3× annual fees super-cap) as a landing zone.
